vi.B: Lời các nhà tiên tri cũng phù hợp với điều này, như đã chép:
vi.R: Điều này đúng như các nhà tiên tri của Đức Chúa Trời đã nói từ xưa. Kinh Thánh chép:

ko.L: 그리고 예언자들의 말씀도 이것과 일치합니다. 기록된 대로입니다.
ko.B: 예언자들의 말씀도 이와 일치합니다. 이렇게 기록되어 있습니다.
ko.R: 이것은 오래전에 하나님의 예언자들이 한 말과 똑같습니다. 성경은 이렇게 말합니다.

decisions.choice: the prophets: the book of the twelve prophets, or the prophets in general
decisions.reason: James quotes Amos, but says "the prophets". The twelve shorter prophets were kept as one book (7:42 calls it "the book of the prophets"), and other prophets also foresaw the nations turning to God (Isaiah 45:20-23; Zechariah 8:20-23).

decisions.choice: this: what Simeon has told, God taking a people from the Gentiles
decisions.reason: "This" picks up 15:14.

decisions.choice: Scripture says
decisions.reason: Readable puts the formula for a quotation in plain words.

source.text: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἀναστρέψω καὶ ἀνοικοδομήσω τὴν σκηνὴν Δαυὶδ τὴν πεπτωκυῖαν καὶ τὰ κατεσκαμμένα αὐτῆς ἀνοικοδομήσω καὶ ἀνορθώσω αὐτήν, ὅπως ἂν ἐκζητήσωσιν οἱ κατάλοιποι τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὸν κύριον, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἐφ’ οὓς ἐπικέκληται τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐπ’ αὐτούς, λέγει κύριος ποιῶν ταῦτα γνωστὰ ἀπ’ αἰῶνος.

records.literal_gloss: After these things I will return and will rebuild the tabernacle of David which has fallen, and the ruins of it I will rebuild and I will set upright it, \v 17 so that may seek out the remnant of men the Lord, and all the Gentiles upon whom has been called the name of Me upon them, says [the] Lord doing these things \v 18 known from eternity.

en.L: 'After these things I will return, and I will rebuild the tent of David which has fallen, and its ruins I will rebuild, and I will set it up again, \v 17 so that the rest of {{gender:people|men}} may seek the Lord, and all the nations upon whom {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name has been called, says [the] Lord, who does these things, \v 18 known from long ago.'
en.B: 'After this I will come back, and I will build again the fallen tent of David. I will build again its ruins and raise it up once more, \v 17 so that the rest of humankind may seek the Lord, all the nations that are called by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, says the Lord, who does these things, \v 18 things made known long ago.'
en.R: 'Later I will come back. David's family is like a tent that has fallen down, but I will build it again. I will rebuild what was ruined and make it stand again. \v 17 Then all other people will look for the Lord. All the nations that I have called {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own will look for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. The Lord says this, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do these things. \v 18 He made them known long ago.'

fr.L: “Après ces choses je reviendrai, et je rebâtirai la tente de David qui est tombée, et ses ruines je [les] rebâtirai, et je la relèverai, \v 17 afin que le reste des {{gender:humains|hommes}} cherche le Seigneur, ainsi que toutes les nations sur lesquelles {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom a été invoqué, dit le Seigneur, qui fait ces choses \v 18 connues depuis toujours.”
fr.B: “Après cela, je reviendrai et je rebâtirai la tente de David qui s’est effondrée. J’en rebâtirai les ruines et je la relèverai, \v 17 afin que le reste de l’humanité cherche le Seigneur, toutes les nations qui portent {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, dit le Seigneur, qui fait ces choses, \v 18 des choses connues depuis longtemps.”
fr.R: “Plus tard, je reviendrai. La famille de David est comme une tente qui est tombée, mais je la rebâtirai. Je reconstruirai ce qui était en ruine et je la ferai tenir debout de nouveau. \v 17 Alors tous les autres humains chercheront le Seigneur. Toutes les nations que j’ai appelées à {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartenir {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} chercheront. C’est le Seigneur qui le dit, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fera ces choses. \v 18 Il les a fait connaître il y a longtemps.”

es.L: “Después de estas cosas volveré, y reedificaré la tienda de David que ha caído, y sus ruinas reedificaré, y la levantaré de nuevo, \v 17 para que el resto de {{gender:la gente|los hombres}} busque al Señor, y todas las naciones sobre las cuales ha sido invocado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, dice [el] Señor, que hace estas cosas, \v 18 conocidas desde antiguo”.
es.B: “Después de esto volveré y reconstruiré la tienda caída de David. Reconstruiré sus ruinas y la volveré a levantar, \v 17 para que el resto de la humanidad busque al Señor, todas las naciones que llevan {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, dice el Señor, que hace estas cosas, \v 18 cosas dadas a conocer desde hace mucho tiempo”.
es.R: “Más tarde volveré. La familia de David es como una tienda que se ha caído, pero yo la levantaré de nuevo. Reconstruiré lo que quedó en ruinas y haré que se mantenga en pie otra vez. \v 17 Entonces toda la demás gente buscará al Señor. Todas las naciones que yo he llamado {{deity_pronoun:mías|Mías}} {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} buscarán. Esto dice el Señor, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hará estas cosas. \v 18 Él las dio a conocer hace mucho tiempo”.

sw.L: 'Baada ya mambo haya nitarudi, nami nitaijenga tena hema ya Daudi iliyoanguka, na magofu yake nitayajenga tena, nami nitaisimamisha tena, \v 17 ili watu waliobaki wamtafute Bwana, na mataifa yote ambayo juu yao jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} limeitwa, asema Bwana, afanyaye mambo haya, \v 18 yaliyojulikana tangu zamani.'
sw.B: 'Baada ya hayo nitarudi, nami nitaijenga upya hema ya Daudi iliyoanguka. Nitayajenga upya magofu yake na kuisimamisha tena, \v 17 ili wanadamu wengine wote wamtafute Bwana, yaani mataifa yote yanayoitwa kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, asema Bwana, anayefanya mambo haya, \v 18 mambo yaliyojulikana tangu zamani.'
sw.R: 'Baadaye nitarudi. Jamaa ya Daudi ni kama hema iliyoanguka chini, lakini nitaijenga tena. Nitajenga upya kile kilichoharibiwa, na kukisimamisha tena. \v 17 Ndipo watu wengine wote watamtafuta Bwana. Mataifa yote ambayo nimeyaita kuwa yangu {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} yatamtafuta. Bwana anasema hivyo, naye atafanya mambo haya. \v 18 Aliyajulisha tangu zamani.'

vi.L: 'Sau những điều này {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trở lại, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ xây lại lều của Đa-vít đã đổ, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ xây lại những chỗ đổ nát của nó, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ dựng nó lên lại, \v 17 để những người còn lại của loài người tìm kiếm Chúa, và mọi dân tộc được gọi bằng danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, Chúa phán, Đấng làm những điều này, \v 18 [những điều] đã được biết từ xưa.'
vi.B: 'Sau đó {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trở lại, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ xây lại lều đã đổ của Đa-vít. Ta sẽ xây lại những chỗ đổ nát của nó và dựng nó lên lại, \v 17 để những người còn lại của nhân loại tìm kiếm Chúa, tức là mọi dân tộc được gọi bằng danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Chúa là Đấng làm những điều này phán vậy, \v 18 những điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã cho biết từ xưa.'
vi.R: 'Sau này {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trở lại. Dòng dõi của Đa-vít giống như một cái lều đã sụp đổ, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ xây lại. Ta sẽ xây lại những gì đã đổ nát và làm cho nó đứng vững trở lại. \v 17 Bấy giờ mọi người khác sẽ tìm kiếm Chúa. Mọi dân tộc mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã gọi là dân của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ tìm kiếm {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Chúa phán như vậy, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ làm những điều này. \v 18 Ngài đã cho biết những điều ấy từ xưa.'

ko.L: '이 일들 뒤에 내가 돌아와서, 무너진 다윗의 장막을 다시 세우고, 그 허물어진 곳들을 다시 세워서, 그것을 바로 일으킬 것이다. \v 17 그리하여 남은 사람들이 주님을 찾고, 내 이름으로 불리는 모든 민족이 [주님을 찾게 할 것이다]. 이 일들을 행하시는 주님께서 말씀하신다. \v 18 [이 일들은] 오래전부터 알려진 것이다.'
ko.B: '그 뒤에 내가 돌아와서, 무너진 다윗의 장막을 다시 짓겠다. 허물어진 곳을 다시 짓고, 그것을 다시 일으켜 세우겠다. \v 17 그리하여 남은 모든 사람이 주님을 찾고, 내 이름으로 불리는 모든 민족도 주님을 찾게 하겠다. 이 일들을 행하시는 주님께서 말씀하신다. \v 18 이것은 오래전부터 알려 주신 일이다.'
ko.R: '나중에 내가 다시 돌아오겠다. 다윗의 집안은 무너진 장막과 같지만, 내가 그것을 다시 세우겠다. 무너진 것을 다시 짓고, 다시 서게 하겠다. \v 17 그러면 다른 모든 사람도 주님을 찾을 것이다. 내 백성으로 부른 모든 민족이 주님을 찾을 것이다. 주님께서 이렇게 말씀하시고, 이 일들을 이루실 것이다. \v 18 주님께서는 오래전에 이 일들을 알려 주셨다.'

decisions.choice: Amos 9:11-12, quoted in the form of the Greek Old Testament
alternatives: a quotation of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: James's words follow the old Greek translation of Amos, not the Hebrew. In the Hebrew, God rebuilds David's fallen booth so that Israel may possess what is left of Edom and all the nations called by his name. The Greek has "so that the rest of humankind may seek". The Hebrew words for "Edom" and "humankind" are written with almost the same letters, and so are the verbs "possess" and "seek"; the Greek translators read them the second way. Both forms say that the nations will come under the name of Israel's God, which is James's point. The opening words "After these things I will return" stand for Amos's "On that day I will raise up", and may echo Jeremiah 12:15.

decisions.choice: the fallen tent of David: David's royal house and kingdom, brought low
decisions.reason: In Amos the "booth" or "hut" of David is his dynasty, fallen like a shelter in ruins. Its rebuilding is the promise of a king from David's line (2 Samuel 7:11-16). Acts sees the promise kept in Jesus, raised to David's throne (2:30-36, 13:32-37).

decisions.choice: the Lord: in Amos the divine name of Israel's God
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Amos 9:12 the speaker is the Lord, written with the divine name, as is usual in the prophets' "says the LORD". The Greek translation uses the word "Lord" for it.

decisions.choice: on whom my name has been called: who belong to God as his own
alternatives: who call on the name of God
decisions.reason: To have someone's name called over you means to be owned by him (Deuteronomy 28:10; Jeremiah 14:9).

decisions.choice: people: humankind as a whole, not men only
decisions.reason: The rest of humankind are set beside "all the nations".

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "who does these things, known from long ago"
alternatives: many later manuscripts: "who does all these things. Known to God from long ago are all his works"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, have the longer wording, which makes a separate sentence. The shorter text, found in early manuscripts, joins the words to the quotation and may echo Isaiah 45:21. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Literal: people, with "men" as the alternative; Balanced and Readable: humankind, all other people
decisions.reason: Following the meaning note. Balanced and Readable use words that are inclusive in themselves.

decisions.choice: the Lord
decisions.reason: The Greek has "Lord", so the English does too, as at 2:34; the meaning note gives the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: David's family is like a tent that has fallen down
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture, as the meaning note does.

decisions.choice: “ ” for the words of Amos inside James's speech
decisions.reason: James's speech is already inside « », so the prophet's words take the inner French quotation marks, as the English uses single marks.

decisions.choice: la tienda de David
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the ordinary word for a tent, a picture of David's royal house brought low (meaning decision on the fallen tent). "Tabernáculo" would suggest the sanctuary of the wilderness, which is not meant.

decisions.choice: el Señor, no divine_name span
decisions.reason: The Greek quotation has "Lord"; as the English does, Spanish writes "el Señor" with no divine_name span (meaning decision on the Lord in Amos). The quotation inside James's words takes the inner marks “ ”.

decisions.choice: watu waliobaki (L); wanadamu wengine wote (B); watu wengine wote (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Greek means humankind as a whole (meaning decision); "watu" and "wanadamu" already include everyone, so the English gender span has no Swahili counterpart.

decisions.choice: kuwa yangu {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} (R)
decisions.reason: Here "yangu" agrees with the nations, not with a thing God owns, so the span goes on the free pronoun "mimi" that marks the Lord as speaker, as the English Readable marks "my".

decisions.choice: "Ta" for the Lord speaking in the quotation, with the setting span except at the start of a sentence; "phán" for the Lord's saying
decisions.reason: God speaking says "Ta" and the verb is "phán", as the style guide sets for God. The quotation follows the Greek Old Testament wording that Acts quotes, so it is drafted from the Greek here, not from the Hebrew of Amos 9:11-12.

decisions.choice: "loài người" (L), "nhân loại" (B), "mọi người khác" (R), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English Literal
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese words for humankind already include women and men, so there is no second wording.

decisions.choice: "những điều Ngài đã cho biết" (B); "Ngài đã cho biết" (R), naming God as the one who made them known
decisions.reason: Vietnamese reads more clearly with a subject; the meaning decision reads "known from long ago" as part of what the Lord says.

decisions.choice: "남은 사람들" with no gender span; "주님" for the Lord, with no divine_name span; God speaks in 해라체 with "나"
decisions.reason: "사람" already means humankind, men and women (meaning decision), so Korean needs no setting where the English has one. The Greek quotation has "Lord", so Korean says "주님", as the Korean Gospels do in quotations; God's own words take the plain style, as in the Old Testament quotations of the Korean Romans.

decisions.choice: "다윗의 장막" (L, B); "다윗의 집안은 무너진 장막과 같지만" (R)
decisions.reason: "장막" is the word for a tent used for living in, and keeps the picture; Readable says what the picture means, as the English Readable does.

source.text: διὸ ἐγὼ κρίνω μὴ παρενοχλεῖν τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐπιστρέφουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν, ἀλλὰ ἐπιστεῖλαι αὐτοῖς τοῦ ἀπέχεσθαι τῶν ἀλισγημάτων τῶν εἰδώλων καὶ τῆς πορνείας καὶ τοῦ πνικτοῦ καὶ τοῦ αἵματος·

records.literal_gloss: Therefore I judge not to trouble those who from the Gentiles are turning to the God, \v 20 but to write to them to abstain from the pollutions of the idols and the sexual immorality and the [thing] strangled and the blood.

en.L: Therefore I judge that we should not trouble those of the Gentiles who are turning to God, \v 20 but should write to them to abstain from the pollutions of idols and from sexual immorality and from what is strangled and from blood.
en.B: So my judgment is that we should not make things hard for the Gentiles who are turning to God. \v 20 Instead we should write to them that they keep away from what idols have defiled, from sexual immorality, from what has been strangled, and from blood.
en.R: So I think that we should not make it hard for the Gentiles who are turning to God. \v 20 Instead, we should write a letter to them. We should tell them not to eat food that has been offered to idols, which makes it unclean. They must not take part in sexual sins. They must not eat meat from animals that were strangled, with the blood still in them. And they must not eat blood.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi moi, je juge qu’il ne faut pas importuner ceux des nations qui se tournent vers Dieu, \v 20 mais leur écrire de s’abstenir des souillures des idoles et de l’immoralité sexuelle et de ce qui est étouffé et du sang.
fr.B: Mon avis est donc qu’il ne faut pas rendre les choses difficiles aux non-Juifs qui se tournent vers Dieu. \v 20 Écrivons-leur plutôt qu’ils se gardent de ce que les idoles ont souillé, de l’immoralité sexuelle, des animaux étouffés et du sang.
fr.R: Je pense donc que nous ne devons pas rendre les choses difficiles aux non-Juifs qui se tournent vers Dieu. \v 20 Nous devrions plutôt leur écrire une lettre. Nous devrions leur dire de ne pas manger de nourriture offerte aux idoles, car elle est impure. Ils ne doivent pas commettre de péchés sexuels. Ils ne doivent pas manger la viande d’animaux étouffés, dont le sang est resté à l’intérieur. Et ils ne doivent pas manger de sang.

es.L: Por lo cual yo juzgo que no se debe molestar a los que de entre los gentiles se convierten a Dios, \v 20 sino escribirles que se abstengan de las contaminaciones de los ídolos, y de la inmoralidad sexual, y de lo estrangulado, y de la sangre.
es.B: Por eso mi parecer es que no debemos ponerles dificultades a los gentiles que se vuelven a Dios. \v 20 Más bien debemos escribirles que se aparten de lo que ha sido contaminado por los ídolos, de la inmoralidad sexual, de lo estrangulado y de la sangre.
es.R: Por eso creo que no debemos hacerles las cosas difíciles a los gentiles que se vuelven a Dios. \v 20 Más bien, debemos escribirles una carta. Debemos decirles que no coman alimentos que han sido ofrecidos a los ídolos, porque eso los hace impuros. Que no tengan relaciones sexuales prohibidas. Que no coman carne de animales estrangulados, con la sangre todavía dentro. Y que no coman sangre.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo mimi naamua kwamba tusiwasumbue wale wa mataifa wanaomgeukia Mungu, \v 20 bali tuwaandikie kwamba wajiepushe na unajisi wa sanamu, na uasherati, na [nyama ya mnyama] aliyenyongwa, na damu.
sw.B: Basi uamuzi wangu ni kwamba tusiwawekee magumu watu wa mataifa wanaomgeukia Mungu. \v 20 Badala yake tuwaandikie kwamba wajiepushe na vitu vilivyotiwa unajisi na sanamu, na uasherati, na nyama ya wanyama walionyongwa, na damu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nadhani hatupaswi kuwawekea magumu watu wa mataifa wanaomgeukia Mungu. \v 20 Badala yake, tuwaandikie barua. Tuwaambie wasile chakula kilichotolewa kwa sanamu, kwa sababu kimekuwa najisi. Wasishiriki katika dhambi za zinaa. Wasile nyama ya wanyama walionyongwa, ambayo bado ina damu ndani yake. Na wasinywe damu.

vi.L: Vì vậy, tôi phán đoán rằng chúng ta đừng gây khó khăn cho những người trong các dân ngoại đang quay về với Đức Chúa Trời, \v 20 nhưng hãy viết cho họ phải kiêng những thứ bị ô uế bởi thần tượng, sự gian dâm, thịt thú vật chết ngạt, và huyết.
vi.B: Vì vậy, theo ý tôi, chúng ta đừng làm khó cho những người ngoại đang quay về với Đức Chúa Trời. \v 20 Thay vào đó, chúng ta nên viết thư bảo họ tránh những gì đã bị ô uế vì thần tượng, tránh gian dâm, tránh thịt thú vật chết ngạt và tránh huyết.
vi.R: Vì vậy tôi nghĩ chúng ta không nên làm khó cho những người ngoại đang quay về với Đức Chúa Trời. \v 20 Thay vào đó, chúng ta nên viết thư cho họ. Chúng ta nên bảo họ đừng ăn đồ ăn đã cúng cho thần tượng, vì đồ ăn ấy bị ô uế. Họ không được phạm tội tình dục. Họ không được ăn thịt thú vật bị chết ngạt mà máu vẫn còn trong thịt. Và họ không được ăn huyết.

ko.L: 그러므로 내 판단으로는, 이방 사람들 가운데서 하나님께 돌아오는 사람들을 괴롭게 하지 말고, \v 20 그들에게 편지를 보내어 우상들로 더러워진 것과 음행과 목 졸라 죽인 것과 피를 멀리하라고 해야 합니다.
ko.B: 그러므로 내 판단은, 하나님께 돌아오는 이방 사람들을 어렵게 하지 말자는 것입니다. \v 20 그 대신에 그들에게 편지를 써서, 우상으로 더러워진 것과 음행과 목 졸라 죽인 것과 피를 멀리하라고 합시다.
ko.R: 그래서 나는 하나님께 돌아오는 유대인이 아닌 사람들을 힘들게 하지 말아야 한다고 생각합니다. \v 20 그 대신에 그들에게 편지를 써서 이렇게 말합시다. 우상에게 바친 음식은 더러워졌으니 먹지 마십시오. 성적으로 죄를 짓는 일에 끼지 마십시오. 목을 졸라 죽여서 피가 그대로 남아 있는 짐승의 고기를 먹지 마십시오. 그리고 피를 먹지 마십시오.

decisions.choice: I judge: I give my verdict
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to give an opinion or to make a ruling. James speaks as a leader proposing a decision, but the letter says it seemed good to the apostles, the elders and the whole church (15:22, 15:25), so the decision was shared.

decisions.choice: the four things: what the law asked of foreigners living among Israel
decisions.reason: Leviticus 17-18 lays down rules for "the foreigner who lives among you" as well as for Israel: no sacrifices to other gods (17:7-9), no eating of blood (17:10-12), meat from animals properly drained of blood (17:13-14), and no forbidden sexual unions (18:6-26). The four requirements match these closely. Kept by Gentile believers, they made it possible for Jewish and Gentile believers to share life and meals.

decisions.choice: the pollutions of idols: food from sacrifices to idols, defiled by them
decisions.reason: The letter names this as "things sacrificed to idols" (15:29, 21:25). Paul deals with the same question in 1 Corinthians 8-10.

decisions.choice: sexual immorality: sexual relations outside marriage, or unions the law forbids
decisions.reason: The word covers every kind of sexual sin. Some take it here to mean the marriages between close relatives forbidden in Leviticus 18, since the other three requirements are about food and the law, but the word is wider than that.

decisions.choice: what is strangled: meat from animals killed without draining the blood
decisions.reason: An animal strangled or caught in a snare still had its blood in it, which the law forbade (Leviticus 17:13-14; Deuteronomy 12:16, 12:23).

decisions.choice: blood: eating or drinking blood
decisions.reason: The law forbade eating blood, because the life is in the blood (Genesis 9:4; Leviticus 17:11). In the Western form of the text, which drops "what is strangled" (see the next note), "blood" can be read as murder.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: four requirements, with "what is strangled"
alternatives: Codex Bezae and other Western witnesses: no "what is strangled", and the added words "and not to do to others what they would not want done to themselves"
decisions.reason: In the Western text, mainly Codex Bezae, the list is three: idols, sexual immorality and blood. Without "strangled" the list can be read as rules of conduct (idolatry, sexual sin, murder), and the added saying, a form of the Golden Rule put negatively, fits that reading. The same changes are found in 15:29. The four-part list stands in the other manuscripts. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: not to eat food offered to idols; meat from animals that were strangled, with the blood still in them
alternatives: to abstain from the pollutions of idols ... what is strangled and blood
decisions.reason: Readable says what each requirement meant, as the meaning notes explain.

decisions.choice: I think
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word; the meaning note explains its weight.

decisions.choice: ce qui est étouffé (L); les animaux étouffés (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Étouffé" is the usual French word for an animal killed without its blood being drained (m5), and it is the term readers will meet in other French works; Readable adds what it meant, as the English does.

decisions.choice: inmoralidad sexual (L, B); relaciones sexuales prohibidas (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the Spanish New Testament (1 Corinthians 5:1, Revelation 2:14); "fornicación" is narrower and old-fashioned. The word covers relations outside marriage and unions the law forbids (meaning decision on sexual immorality), which Readable says plainly.

decisions.choice: lo estrangulado
decisions.reason: Spanish keeps the short neuter phrase at Literal and Balanced, as the English "what is strangled"; Readable explains it as meat with the blood still in it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: uasherati (L, B); dhambi za zinaa (R)
decisions.reason: Sexual relations outside marriage or unions the law forbids (meaning decision): "uasherati" is the broad word, as in 1 Corinthians 5:1; Readable says "dhambi za zinaa" (sexual sins), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: [nyama ya mnyama] aliyenyongwa (L); nyama ya wanyama walionyongwa (B)
decisions.reason: Meat from animals killed without draining the blood (meaning decision); Swahili needs the noun, supplied in brackets at Literal.

decisions.choice: "sự gian dâm" (L), "gian dâm" (B), "phạm tội tình dục" (R) for sexual immorality
decisions.reason: "gian dâm" covers sexual relations outside marriage, as the meaning decision says; Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: "thịt thú vật chết ngạt" and "huyết"
decisions.reason: "huyết" is the word the law uses for blood that may not be eaten; Readable explains the strangled animal with "máu", the plain word, as the English Readable explains it.

decisions.choice: "음행" (L, B); "성적으로 죄를 짓는 일" (R) for sexual immorality
decisions.reason: "간음" is adultery only; "음행" covers sexual relations outside marriage and the unions the law forbids, as the meaning decision describes. Readable says it in plain words.

source.text: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ ἐκ γενεῶν ἀρχαίων κατὰ πόλιν τοὺς κηρύσσοντας αὐτὸν ἔχει ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον ἀναγινωσκόμενος.

records.literal_gloss: Moses for from generations of old in every city [ones] proclaiming him has, in the synagogues on every Sabbath being read.

en.L: For Moses from ancient generations has in every city those who proclaim him, being read in the synagogues every Sabbath."
en.B: For Moses has been preached in every town since generations long past, and he is read aloud in the synagogues every Sabbath."
en.R: For a very long time the law of Moses has been taught in every city. Every Sabbath day people read it aloud in the synagogues."

fr.L: Car Moïse, depuis les générations anciennes, a dans chaque ville des gens qui le prêchent, étant lu dans les synagogues chaque sabbat. »
fr.B: Car depuis des générations, Moïse est prêché dans chaque ville, et on le lit à haute voix dans les synagogues chaque sabbat. »
fr.R: En effet, depuis très longtemps, la Loi de Moïse est enseignée dans toutes les villes. Chaque jour de sabbat, on la lit à haute voix dans les synagogues. »

es.L: Porque Moisés desde generaciones antiguas tiene en cada ciudad quienes lo proclaman, siendo leído en las sinagogas cada sábado».
es.B: Porque desde hace muchas generaciones Moisés ha sido predicado en cada ciudad, y se lee en voz alta en las sinagogas cada sábado».
es.R: Porque desde hace muchísimo tiempo la ley de Moisés se enseña en todas las ciudades. Cada sábado la gente la lee en voz alta en las sinagogas».

sw.L: Kwa maana Musa tangu vizazi vya kale ana katika kila mji watu wanaomhubiri, akisomwa katika masinagogi kila Sabato."
sw.B: Kwa maana tangu vizazi vya zamani Musa amehubiriwa katika kila mji, na maandiko yake yanasomwa kwa sauti katika masinagogi kila Sabato."
sw.R: Kwa muda mrefu sana sheria ya Musa imefundishwa katika kila mji. Kila siku ya Sabato watu huisoma kwa sauti katika masinagogi."

vi.L: Vì từ các thế hệ xa xưa, trong mỗi thành Môi-se đều có người rao giảng, và [sách của ông] được đọc trong các nhà hội mỗi ngày Sa-bát."
vi.B: Vì từ bao đời nay, Môi-se đã được rao giảng trong mọi thành, và sách của ông được đọc lớn tiếng trong các nhà hội mỗi ngày Sa-bát."
vi.R: Vì từ rất lâu rồi, luật pháp Môi-se đã được dạy trong mọi thành. Mỗi ngày Sa-bát, người ta đều đọc lớn luật pháp ấy trong các nhà hội."
